newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia April job ads up a record 16.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia April job ads up a record 16.7 pct.

text.p: The Australian and New Zealand (ANZ) Banking Group said on Monday its job advertisement series rose 16.7 percent in April, the largest monthly increase since the series began in 1975, following a 1.9 percent fall in March.

The jump took job ads to their highest level since January 1996, and they are now 12.9 percent higher than last April. It is the first time since July 1995 that the series has shown an increase over its level of a year before.
The trend series rose by 2.5 percent in April, the largest such increase since July 1994, following a similar increase in March, which was revised up from a 0.4 percent increase.

"The sharp rise in job advertisements in April partly reflects the negative impact on the March figures of the earlier than usual Easter this year, for which the normal seasonal adjustment procedures were not able to correct," ANZ chief economist Saul Eslake said in a statement.

However, the ANZ estimated that even allowing for this effect the number of job ads would have risen by around five percent in April, which still would have been a sizeable increase by historical standards.
"The trend in job advertising over the past few months is consistent with net new job creation averaging around 17,000 per month over the next three months," Eslake said.
This outlook was set to strengthen further unless April's gain was entirely reversed in May and June, he said.

"Thus we should expect to see some improvement in the official employment statistics over the next few months, in contrast to the outright declines in employment reported for February and March," Eslake said.
Those declines were probably best seen as a correction to the "implausibly strong" employment figures of the previous six months, he said.
The improvement was too late to meet the government's forecast of 1.5 percent employment growth in the year to June 30, as that would require growth of 70,000 jobs per month in the June quarter.
"However, it does suggest that employment growth should be on an upward trajectory going into the 1997/98 financial year," Eslake said.
All states and the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) saw job ads rise in April. The ACT led the way with a rise of 25.4 percent, while Tasmania bought up the rear with a 1.5 percent rise.
